verdict.rationale: Proa documents signals inside hydrated RSJS islands, which compile to a small vanilla-JS module with seed state, so declaring reactive state is a first-party capability. The evidence never says that only dependent UI code re-runs when a signal changes, so the fine-grained part of the story is unproven. missing for 10: documentation of signal dependency tracking and fine-grained updates, an explanation of the reactivity model (effects/derived state), independent or hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As a developer, I can declare reactive state and have only the dependent UI code re-run when it changes

citations.quote: Add signals and event handlers, and Proa emits the server-rendered HTML plus the JavaScript required for that island
Each hydrated RSJS island emits a small vanilla-JS module plus seed state, served with a shared runtime around 1.3 KB gzipped.
